source_refs.title: Change the font size on your iPhone, iPad, and iPod touch - Apple Support
source_refs.applicability: iPhone; the change applies in apps that support Dynamic Type, as the page states
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Go to Settings > Display & Brightness, then select Text Size. Drag the slider to select the font size you want. Making the text too large might make it hard to tap buttons or other functions within apps.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On iPhone: Go to Settings > Display & Brightness, then select Text Size. Drag the slider to select the font size you want. You can change the size of your font in Mail, Contacts, Calendar, Phone, Notes, and other apps that support Dynamic Type. Making the text too large might make it hard to tap buttons or other functions within apps.

source_refs.title: Change text & display settings - Android Accessibility Help
source_refs.section: Change font size in Quick Settings (Use Quick Settings to adjust font)
source_refs.applicability: Android; the Font Size tile must be added to Quick Settings first; the page says you can adjust font size up to 200%
source_refs.verified_excerpt: From the top of the screen, swipe down to find Quick Settings. Tap Font Size.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Android: Swipe down from the top of the screen to open Quick Settings. Tap Font Size. Tap Increase or Decrease, or drag the percentage slider left or right. If you haven't added the Font Size tile to Quick Settings, you must add it first. If you adjust the font size from Settings, the Font Size tile will be automatically added in Quick Settings. You can adjust font size up to 200%.

source_refs.title: Make text and apps bigger - Microsoft Support
source_refs.section: Make text bigger on your screen
source_refs.applicability: Windows 11; the page says Windows scales up the size of all text
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Drag the Text size slider to the right to increase the size of the sample text. Once you're happy with the text size, select Apply. Windows scales up the size of all text.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Windows 11: Open Accessibility settings by pressing the Windows logo key+U, or go to Start, then Settings, then Accessibility. Select 'Text size'. Drag the 'Text size' slider to the right to increase the size of the sample text. Once you're happy with the text size, select 'Apply'. Windows scales up the size of all text.
